taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes the former name Common Peafowl was changed to Indian Peafowl (AOU 2012).
fieldMarks: Male: iridescent blue neck and breast, golden back and sides, long train with eye-spots
Female: brown, grey and cream with no train
Juveniles light yellow to brown and resemble the female; males take about 3 years to grow the train
Weighs 2.7-6 kg; both sexes have spurs (Animal Diversity Web)
behavior: Solitary or in small groups outside breeding; roosts in trees, diurnal
Dust-bathes; eats insects, reptiles, seeds and grain
habitat: Open forest, forest edge, second growth, scrub and cultivated land.
range: Native to India and southeastern Asia. Small semi-domesticated populations are introduced and established in scattered North American localities and Hawaii.
